evidence: Sorted card view by Priority ascending then toggled to descending; statusbar showed "Sorted by Priority (ascending/descending)". Switched to table view - sort reset to "Sort" (no active sort) and table sorted independently by Task Name; switching back to Cards retained Priority (descending) sort, confirming independent per-view sort selections.

Selecting Priority in sort dropdown immediately reordered card entries (1,1,2,2,3,42 ascending); statusbar text "Sorted by Priority (ascending)" identified field and direction; clicking again showed "Sorted by Priority (descending)" with reversed order. App remained fully interactive afterward.

After sorting by Priority (asc then desc) and by Task Name, entry count remained "6 entries" throughout and each entry's field values (name, priority, date, completed, notes) were unchanged across sorts - only order changed.
Switched from table to card view: all 6 entries and their field values (Task Name, Priority, Due Date, Completed, Notes) were identical in both views, only presentation changed.

With no sort active, used drag-handle keyboard reordering (Space to pick up, ArrowUp to move, Space to drop) to move "QA Test Entry" earlier in Card view (result: entry-1, QA, entry-2, entry-3, entry-4, entry-5) and independently in Table view (result: entry-1, entry-2, QA, entry-3, entry-4, entry-5). Switching between views preserved each view's own manual order without affecting the other.

issue: New entry not persisted across page reload
actual: Created entry "QA Test Entry" with Priority 42, Due Date Sep 1 2026, Notes "Hello World", Completed=Yes; it appeared immediately (entries count went from 5 to 6) and also a custom "Notes" text field was added. After navigating/reloading the app at http://localhost:6074/, the entry list reverted to the original 5 seed entries and the "Notes" field configuration also disappeared, i.e. no server-side or local persistence occurred.

evidence: Added "Notes" (Text) and "Active" (Checkbox) fields via Configure Fields dialog; both immediately appeared as new columns in the table header, as inputs/toggles in the Add Entry form, and as fields in Card view.

Created entry "QA Test 2" with Task Name text, Priority=7 (number), Due Date=2026-09-10 (date), Completed=checked, Notes="Sample note text" (text), Active=unchecked (checkbox). After saving, table row showed "QA Test 2","7","Sep 10, 2026", check-icon for Completed, "Sample note text", x-icon for Active. Card view (verified earlier with other fields) shows same values with Yes/No labels.

Priority field is a native input[type=number]. Playwright's fill() rejected typing "abc" into it (browser-level error "Cannot type text into input[type=number]"). Forcing the raw value to "abc" via JS and dispatching input event resulted in value reverting to "" (browser-native rejection). Entering valid "7" was accepted and saved correctly.

Due Date field is a native input[type=date]. Forcing an invalid date string "2026-13-45" (month 13, day 45) via JS resulted in the value reverting to "" (native browser rejection). Setting a valid date "2026-09-10" was accepted and correctly saved/displayed as "Sep 10, 2026".

Configure Fields dialog labels the type selector clearly with options Text/Number/Date/Checkbox. Entry form renders type-appropriate controls: Text→textbox, Number→spinbutton(input type=number), Date→input type=date, Checkbox→checkbox toggle with "Yes"/"No" label.

Entry form checkbox toggles show text label "Yes"/"No" beside the checkbox. In Table view, checked values render a green check icon (lucide-check, text-success class) and unchecked/false values render a muted X icon (lucide-x, text-muted-foreground). Card view renders explicit "Yes"/"No" text for checkbox fields.

Both table and card views display identical entries and field values (verified for Task Name, Priority, Due Date, Completed, Notes, Active across 6 entries). Entries lacking a value for a newly-added field show "—" in table cells and "—" in card fields, providing a clear, consistent empty-value indicator in both views.

Searching "marketing" returned 1 matching entry ("Review marketing materials") with statusbar text '1 entry matching "marketing"'. Searching "MARKETING" (uppercase) returned the same 1 match, confirming case-insensitivity. Clearing the search via the clear button restored the count to "6 entries" with all entries visible again.

issue: Quick search matches only raw internal values, not the formatted values shown to users
actual: Searching "Sep 10" (the date format displayed in both table and card views as "Sep 10, 2026") returned 0 matches, while searching the raw internal ISO value "2026-09-10" returned 1 match. Similarly, searching "Yes" (the checkbox state text shown in Card view / meaning of the check icon in Table view for Completed=true, which 3 entries have) returned 0 matches. This shows search only queries raw stored values, not the user-visible formatted date or checkbox-state text.

issue: No filter feature exists in the application
actual: Searched the entire UI (toolbar, table headers, card view, semantic snapshot with hidden elements included, and a DOM-wide scan for any element with "filter" in aria-label/title/text) and found no filter control of any kind. Only a free-text "Search entries..." quick-search box exists; there is no field-specific filter criteria UI, so users cannot define filter criteria or view only matching entries via a filter mechanism.

issue: No filter feature exists to evaluate against this constraint
actual: As found for FT-6, there is no filter UI anywhere in the app (toolbar, table, card view, or DOM-wide search for "filter"-labeled elements all came up empty). Since no filtering functionality exists, entries cannot be filtered by field criteria, so the constraint cannot be satisfied.

issue: No import feature exists in the application
actual: Searched the entire UI (toolbar, Fields dialog, table/card views) and performed a DOM-wide scan for any element with "import" in aria-label/title/text; no import control, button, or file-upload mechanism was found anywhere in the app. Users cannot import data at all, so schema-validated import behavior cannot be exercised.
